content.comment_body: Hi, I'm experiencing an issue with input signals. I created a program for a machine and downloaded it onto the [product_name]. The problem is that the device isn't detecting the inputs. In the online test mode, the inputs remain inactive. When I press the button, I measure 24 VDC at the terminal, but the [product_name] does not register that the button is pressed. I'm unsure if something is not configured properly or if it's another issue. Thanks and sorry for my English, [user_name].

Do you have 24 V power supplied to the [product_name]? If it's a DC version, the leftmost terminal on top should be +, the second one should be -. Input switches need to be connected to the + or the leftmost terminal and an input. Did you set the [product_name] to RUN mode? My English isn't great either...

Hello, Remember to click on the glasses icon while in online test mode. Try building a simple program with one input connected to one output to check if the [product_name] is functioning correctly. Regards,
Also confirm that you are using the 24VDC version of the device.
Can you share the wiring diagram or file you've created?
Hi, please provide your wiring details—I suspect the issue may be related to wiring. [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user is facing difficulty with a [product_name] not registering input signals, even though the correct voltage appears at the terminals when a button is pressed. Several users recommend checking wiring, ensuring the device version is 24VDC, verifying the correct power connections, setting the device to RUN mode, and following proper online test procedures. The issue remains unresolved in the discussion.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that the [product_name] will accurately detect changes in input states when a button is pressed and a voltage is present at the terminal.
